becomes  3rd person singular present of be·come (Verb)


Verb
  1. Begin to be: "they became angry".
  2. Grow to be; turn into.

Verb

The second definition being the important one. 'Turn into' - there is no timelimit on Becoming. It simply turns into this aspect.  That's Read as Written.

And there is a precedent for any card that creates an ongoing effect with no time limit, and that is to end the effect when the card is destroyed.  This is not stated anywhere in the rulebook, but it has been explained by Christopher and Adam (I've never played a game with Paul), and it makes since both commonly and logically.  To interpret 'become' to not only have a time limit, but also to break the precedent of limitless effects removed when the corresponding card is removed, it's not consistant with the rest of the game.

Okay, he's back under the cards and notes, but while we had him in the sunlight Christopher gave us a cryptic message. Once we deciphered it (turns out it was in another language - who knew there were other languages out there?), here's what he said:

When Adaptive Plating Subroutine comes into play, it initially does nothing. It just sits and waits for Omnitron to get hit. Then, when the giant robot does take damage, Adaptive Plating Subroutine kicks in, making Omnitron immune to that type of damage after the damage has been dealt. Then, Adaptive Plating Subroutine sits there, maintaining that damage immunity until another type of damage comes along and changes it. You all seem to understand this just fine, but I wanted to reiterate the basics of how it worked, just so we were all on the same page.

The important distinction here is that Adaptive Plating Subroutine is the thing making Omnitron immune to melee or fire or rabit damage. So, if Adaptive Plating Subroutine is not in play, then Omnitron has no damage immunity.

 

Final answer: When APS goes away, the protection does, also.
